title: At the Doctor's / Akwantu a Adwene Gyinae
bridge: Wɔ Twi mu, sɛ yɛbɛka ho kɔm a, yɛbɔ no ase 'me duele' + sɛɛ a  bodi no (me duele la cabeza). Wɔ English mu, kyerɛw no ntɛm: 'I have' + 'a headache' (tengo un dolor de cabeza). Ɛyɛ nkwa ho nhoahoa pɛn na ɛnte saa 'I hurt my head' sɛ ɛbɛka ho kɔm a. Nso, wɔ English mu, 'hurt' de yɛ ɔkasa: 'My head hurts' (mi cabeza duele). Sɛ wubɛtumi abɔ 'have' ne nnipa a wɔde bɔ ho kɔm no ne 'hurt' ne mmarima no ho ase a, ɛno na ɛbɛma wuka ho te sɛ Englishman.
rule: Sɛ yɛbɛka ho kɔm ne nni a wɔwɔ wɔ A2 animuonyam a, yɛde nnipa a wɔde bɔ ho kɔm no ne mmarima no ho ase: 1) 'I have' + nnipa (a headache, a cold, a fever, a cough, a sore throat, a stomachache, etc.) sɛ wubɛka sɛ woyɛ adwene. 2) 'My [sɛɛ a  bodi no] hurts' anaa 'My [sɛɛ a  bodi no] is sore' sɛ wubɛka sɛ sɛɛ a  bodi no kɔm wɔ wiase. 3) 'I feel' + adwene (sick, dizzy, tired, etc.) sɛ wubɛka sɛ woyɛ adwene. Wɔ mfonini ne mmoa ano a, yɛde 'do/does' (Do you have...? Yes, I do. No, I don't). Sɛ wubɛma obi akannifo a, yɛde 'should' / 'shouldn't' (You should rest, You shouldn't eat spicy food). Sonka sɛ 'hurt' ne ɔkasa a ɛnyɛ nea ɛho hɔ: hurt - hurt - hurt. Wɔmmusɛe 'me duele' te sɛ ɛbɛka ho kɔm a; yɛde mmarima no ho ase: 'My head hurts' (no 'I hurt my head' gyaa na ɛyɛ nkwa). Nso, 'I've got' yɛ ɔkwan a wɔde bɔ 'I have got' (I've got a cold). Wɔ nhoma a wɔde kyerɛw no mu a, wɔde 'I have a cold'.

common_error.explanation: Nkwa a ɛba ne sɛ wɔde 'me duele la cabeza' kyerɛ 'I hurt my head'. Nanso 'hurt' sɛ ɛyɛ ɔkasa a ɛde abɔ a, ɛka sɛ wɔde abɔ wɔn (me lastimé la cabeza). Sɛ wubɛka ho kɔm a, yɛde 'have a headache' anaa 'my head hurts'. Sonka: 'hurt' sɛ ɛyɛ ɔkasa a ɛnyɛ nea ɛho hɔ (sɛ ɛnyɛ nea ɛho hɔ a) ɛka ho kɔm, nanso sɛɛ a  bodi no na ɛyɛ mmarima no (my head hurts). Ma wuhwehwɛ sɛ wubɛde 'have' + nnipa a wɔde bɔ ho kɔm no ho ase sɛ wubɛka ho kɔm a.

examples.original: I have a cold.
examples.note: De 'have' + nni anaa ho kɔm no ho ase. Mmomusɛe 'I am cold' sɛ wubɛka sɛ woyɛ me nni, ɛno ka sɛ woyɛ me nsa.

examples.original: I have a cough and a runny nose.
examples.phonetic: /aɪ hæv ə kɒf ænd ə ˈrʌni noʊz/
examples.translation: Mɛyɛ me gyena ne me su kɔm.
examples.note: Sɛ wubɛka nni ne ho kɔm no a, yɛde 'and' de wɔn bɔ: cough and runny nose. Hwehwɛ sɛ 'runny nose' (gyena a ɛtɔ).

examples.original: I feel dizzy.
examples.note: De 'feel' + adwene sɛ wubɛka sɛ woyɛ adwene. Wɔ Twi mu yɛde 'me yɛ me ho', nanso wɔ English mu wɔmmusɛe 'I feel me'.

examples.original: Take this medicine twice a day.
examples.translation: Sɛe adwene a ɛyɛ ɔha ne mmienu da.
examples.note: De 'take' sɛ wubɛka sɛ wubɛsɛe adwene, ɛmmusɛe 'drink' (sɛe). 'Twice a day' ka sɛ wɔda ne mmienu.

examples.original: You should rest in bed.
examples.translation: Sɛ wubɛsɛe a, fa akɔntɔ ne din.
examples.note: Sɛ wubɛma obi akannifo a, de 'should' + ɔkasa a ɛnyɛ nea ɛho hɔ. Ɛho hɔ pii pɛn na 'must' (nkwa).

examples.original: I need to make an appointment.
examples.translation: Mepɛ sɛ mɛbɛma wɔn akɔntɔ ne din.
examples.note: De 'make an appointment' sɛ wubɛka sɛ wubɛma wɔn akɔntɔ ne din. 'Need to' + ɔkasa ka sɛ wopɛ.

examples.original: My back hurts a lot.
examples.translation: Me nsa kɔm mfe a mɛbɛ.
examples.note: De 'a lot' ahyia anaa ahyia ɔkasa no. Mmomusɛe 'my back hurts much' gyaa na wode 'a'.

examples.original: I have a sharp pain in my chest.
examples.phonetic: /aɪ hæv ə ʃɑːrp peɪn ɪn maɪ tʃɛst/
examples.translation: Mɛyɛ me kɔm a ɛtɔ wɔ me nsa mu.
examples.note: De 'sharp' sɛ wubɛka sɛ kɔm no tɔ, na 'dull' sɛ wubɛka sɛ kɔm no nyɛ. Ka sɛ woyɛ he a wɔde 'in my + sɛɛ a  bodi no'.

examples.original: My knee is swollen and red.
examples.note: De 'is' + adwene sɛ wubɛka sɛ woyɛ adwene. Sonka sɛ 'swollen' ne adwene a ɛnyɛ nea ɛho hɔ.

title: Booking Accommodation / Kyɛfa ahoɔden
bridge: Wɔ Twi, yɛnka ‘kyɛfa’ ho abɔ kɛse, sɛ ‘Mɛkyɛfa ahoɔden bi’, nanso wɔ English, ɛsɛ sɛ woatwa ‘would like’ ne ‘to book’ ma w’akyi yɛ adwuma a ɛyɛ nkwa. Enti, sɛ wopɛ sɛ woka ho asɛm biara a ɛyɛ ɛkwan a ɛfiri so akyi, na woyɛ adwuma a ɛyɛ nkwa, ɛsɛ sɛ woyɛ adwuma a ɛyɛ nkwa. Ɛsɛ sɛ woyɛ adwuma a ɛyɛ nkwa.
rule: Saa wopɛ sɛ wokyɛfa ahoɔden wɔ English a, hwɛ sɛ woyɛ adwuma a ɛyɛ nkwa sɛ: ‘I would like to book...’ (Mɛpɛ sɛ mekyɛfa...), ‘I'd like to make a reservation’ (Mɛpɛ sɛ mɛbɔ kyɛfa). Wɔhwehwɛ sɛ woyɛ adwuma a ɛyɛ nkwa sɛ ‘My name is...’. Ma w’akyi yɛ adwuma a ɛyɛ nkwa ma w’akyi yɛ adwuma a ɛyɛ nkwa. Ma w’akyi yɛ adwuma a ɛyɛ nkwa. Ma w’akyi yɛ adwuma a ɛyɛ nkwa.

common_error.explanation: Wɔ Twi, yɛka ‘mɛpɛ sɛ mekyɛfa’ ne ‘pɛ’ asɛm, nanso wɔ English, ‘want’ asɛm yɛ ɔkwan a ɛyɛ den sɛn na ɛnyɛ nkwa. title: At the Bank or Exchange Office / Banku anaa Ntɛm Nyinaa Aheman mu
bridge: Akan asɛm mu, sɛ wopɛ sɛ woka sɛm kɛse a, waka 'Mepɛ sɛ... ' anaa 'Womfa me... ?', nanso Twi mu yɛnka 'Mepɛ... ' anaa 'Mefa me... ?'. Anidaso no, wubetumi ase wɔ Twi mu sɛ woka 'Mepɛ sɛ mefa... ' anaa 'Womfa me... ?'. Na wɔ Twi mu,  'can' ne 'would' mmfata ako a wɔde bɔ kyerɛw kronkron. Enti, wɔ Twi mu, sɛ wopɛ sɛ woka sɛm kɛse a, waka 'Mepɛ sɛ mefa... ' anaa 'Womfa me... ?'.
rule: Sɛ wopɛ sɛ woyi ntɛm banku anaa ntɛm nyinaa aheman mu a, wabɛ ka asɛm kɛse a wɔde bɔ kyerɛw kronkron. Sɛ wopɛ sɛ woka sɛm kɛse a, waka 'Mepɛ sɛ mefa... ' anaa 'Womfa me... ?'. Enti, sɛ wopɛ sɛ woka sɛm kɛse a, waka 'Mepɛ sɛ mefa... ' anaa 'Womfa me... ?'. Na wɔ Twi mu,  'can' ne 'would' mmfata ako a wɔde bɔ kyerɛw kronkron.

title: Job Interview Basics / Nkyerɛaseɛ Wɔ Akwanmu Akɔntɔso
bridge: Wɔ Akwanmu Akɔntɔso tweasɛm mu wɔ Englizi, asɛm a wɔrebisa no yɛ mfatoho na yɛ ntɛm. Enti wɔntumi bu twitwafo no ho nhwɛso a ɛyɛ formal anaa informal; nyinaa yɛ 'you'. Anaa, ɛsɛ sɛ wɔde present simple bɔ asɛm a ɛbɛka ho nhia wɔ hɔ na wɔde past simple bɔ asɛm a ɛbɛka ho nhia wɔ hɔ. Hwɛ sɛ wɔntumi bu 'do/does' a wɔde bisa asɛm, na ɛno ara na ɛyɛ wɔ Twi.
rule: Sɛ wopɛ sɛ woka wo ho asɛm, de 'I am' (me yɛ) na 'I have' (me wɔ). Sɛ wopɛ sɛ woka sɛdeɛ woyɛ no, de present simple: 'I work as...' (mewɔ hwɛfoɔ...). Sɛ wopɛ sɛ woka wo nneɛma a ɛda no, de past simple: 'I worked at...' (mewɔ hwɛfoɔ wɔ...). Asɛm a wɔrebisa no ne: 'What do you do?' (Deɛ woyɛ no?), 'Why do you want this job?' (Naasei wopɛ sɛ woakɔ yɛ no?), 'What are your strengths?' (Deɛ wɔyɛ den no?). Twe ntumi sɛ wɔ Englizi no mu no, wɔnnyɛ nea wɔde fa so.

title: At the post office / Nkyɛ post office no
bridge: Wɔ Twi, sɛ wopɛ sɛ woaboa mmara ne kɔhwɛ kwan wɔ post office, woatwa mmara bɛka 'Mepɛ sɛ mefa' anaa 'Mepɛ sɛ mebɔ', na wɔ Twi yɛ mmara a ɛso wɔhwehwɛ sɛ 'Mepɛ sɛ mefa' anaa 'Mepɛ sɛ mebɔ'. Afei, wɔ Twi, mmara 'send' twa 'to' ma wɔkɔfa kwan (send something to someone), na wɔ Twi yɛ 'fa biribi ma obi'. Hwɛ ma wɔnni nsɛm pii wɔ kyerɛw wɔkɔtɔn so, sɛ 'How much does it cost?', na wɔ Twi yɛ 'Wode wɔn pɛn ni?'.
rule: Sɛ wopɛ sɛ woka fa kwan ne post services wɔ Twi wɔ A2 level no, twa mmara yi: 1) 'Mepɛ sɛ mefa + mmara' (Mepɛ sɛ mefa + infinitive) ma woka pɛsɛm, sɛ 'Mepɛ sɛ mefa pakage yi.' 2) 'Mepɛ sɛ mebɔ + mmara' (Mepɛ sɛ mebɔ + infinitive) ma woka kɔhwɛ kwan a ɛyɛ pa, sɛ 'Mepɛ sɛ mebɔ some stamps.' 3) 'Wode wɔn pɛn ni?' ne 'Wode wɔn pɛn ni?' ma wɔhwɛ kwan wɔ prices, sɛ 'Wode shipping pɛn ni?' 4) Twa 'to' akyi mmara sɛ 'send' ne 'mail' ma wɔkɔfa kwan, sɛ 'Send it to my friend.' 5) Kyerɛw wɔ 'where' ne 'when' ma wɔkɔhwɛ kwan wɔ services, sɛ 'Where can I pick up my package?' Nka sɛ wɔ Twi, adjective twa noun anim (registered mail), na wɔ Spanish no adjective twa noun akyi (correo certificado).

title: Renting a Flat / Pɔ ahyɛse
bridge: Wɔ Twi, sɛ yɛbɛka ho nhia a, yɛbɛka 'pɔ' anaa 'ahyɛ', na sɛ yɛbɛka sɛ ahyɛse bi wɔ a, yɛbɛka 'wɔ nea ɛwɔ' anaa 'wɔ ahyɛ'. Wɔ English, yɛbɛka 'rent' ma ɔkɔ so verb ne noun ('rent' = ahyɛ), na 'available' anaa 'for rent' ma yɛbɛka sɛ ɛwɔ. Fa akɔnta ahyɛse: wɔ English, yɛbɛka 'rent an apartment' (biara nni ahyɛse), nanso wɔ Twi, yɛbɛka 'pɔ ahyɛse'. Ansa na wɔ English, anaafoɔ no biara wɔ 'is for rent' anaa 'is available' a ɛde bɔ nea wɔ Twi, ɛde bɔ 'wɔ ahyɛ' anaa 'wɔ nea ɛwɔ'.
rule: Sɛ wɔbɛka ho nhia wɔ English A2 a, ehia wo sɛ wɔhu: (1) Verb 'to rent' (pɔ) ne ne nimdefoɔ: rent / rents / renting / rented. (2) Ahyɛse 'for' ma noun 'rent' ma wɔbɛka sɛ biribi wɔ ahyɛ: 'for rent' (wɔ ahyɛ). (3) Adjective 'available' (wɔ nea ɛwɔ) ma wɔbɛka sɛ ahyɛse bi wɔ. (4) Kyɛfa bi a ɛso: 'apartment' (ahyɛse), 'flat' (ahyɛse, ɛso wɔ British English), 'landlord' (ahyeɛfoɔ), 'tenant' (ahyeɛfoɔ), 'deposit' (ahyɛse sika), 'rent' (ahyɛse sika a ɛyɛ me), 'lease' (ahyɛse akwan). (5) Sɛ wɔbɛka ho asɛm a, hwehwɛ 'How much is the rent?' (Ahyɛse sika no adu ne?) na 'Is it furnished?' (Ɛyɛ furniture?). Wɔ akwan no, nka sɛ wɔ English, adjectives no wɔ nouns anim: 'a small apartment', ɛnyɛ 'an apartment small'.

title: Making small talk at a party / Kasa nkyerɛkyerɛ ano asɛm wɔ akwantu mu
bridge: Wɔ Twi mu, bere a yɛbɛka akwantu, yɛbɛka 'ɛnte sɛn?' anaa 'wo ho te sɛn?' na yɛnka 'te' kyerɛ sɛ yɛwɔ asɛm biara mu. Wɔ English mu, yɛka 'How are you?' anaa 'How's it going?' anaa 'What's up?' sɛ yɛwɔ ano asɛm mu. Nya da sɛ wɔ English mu, wɔnka 'I agree' na wɔnka 'I am agree' (sɛnea wɔka wɔ Twi mu). Sɛ wubɛma adwuma a, ka 'Would you like something to drink?' anaa 'Do you want a drink?' Sɛ wubɛka sɛ wopɛ anaa wopɛn a, ka 'I like...' anaa 'I don't like...'. Sɛ wubɛka sɛ woyɛ nokware a, ka 'I agree with you'. Sɛ wɔbɛka 'How are you?' a, ka 'I'm good', 'I'm fine', anaa 'Pretty good'. Sɛ wubɛfa a, ka 'It was nice talking to you' anaa 'See you later'.

title: Complaining and Apologizing / Kɔhwɛ ne maaforo
bridge: Wɔ Twi, woyɛ 'maaforo' anaa 'me ntease' ma w’adwene, nanso wɔ Twirekron mu, mmara biara wɔ: 'I'm sorry' yɛ ma yɛnkyɛ de anaa yɛnkyɛ a ɛyɛ den paa, na 'excuse me' yɛ ma kɔhwɛ anaa maaforo a ɛyɛ ntɛm. Enti, wɔ kɔhwɛ mu, Twirekron tumi de ‘can't’ anaa ‘won't’ maa ɛkɔ so atɛn, nanso wɔ Twi, ɛbɛka ‘mmom’ anaa ‘wɔn mmom’ a ɛyɛ kwan paa. Hwɛ kwan ma w’asɛm ne ma w’atɛn a wode ‘to’ a ɛba n’adwene ‘sorry’ so.
rule: Ma w’akɔhwɛ wɔ Twirekron mu, ɛbɔ ‘I can't + verb’ (memmɔ) anaa ‘This is + adjective’ (ɛyɛ). Ma w’amaaforo, de ‘I'm sorry (for) + gerund’ anaa ‘I apologize for + noun’. Nhoma ‘sorry’ a ɛba ‘for’ so ma w’akomaa (I'm sorry for being late). Wɔ nkyɛn a ɛyɛ den paa, ‘I apologize’ yɛ den paa. Ma w’asomdwoeɛ, ɛbɔ ‘It's okay’, ‘No problem’, anaa ‘That's fine’. Mmom ‘I'm sorry’ nni ma w’akɔfa (de ‘excuse me’).

title: Describing your hometown / Kasa kuan mu nwoma ne nniee
bridge: Wɔ Twirekronkan, sɛ wopɛ sɛ woka kuan mu nwoma ne nniee no, woyɛ ‘to be’ de ka nea ɛte (big, small, quiet) ne ‘there is/there are’ ma woka sɛ wɔyɛ dɛn. Wɔ Hɔspansakan mu no, woka ‘es grande’ anaa ‘hay un parque’, nanso wɔ Twirekronkan mu no, nka ‘there is’ kyerɛ sɛ ɛyɛ nkɔsoɔ ne ‘there are’ kyerɛ sɛ ɛyɛ mmiɛnsa. Enti, sɛnea woakyerɛdeɛ no yɛ no yɛ dɛn so ara na ɛsɛ: kyerɛdeɛ no ntam ne deɛ ɛkasa no akyi, sɛnea ɛte wɔ ‘My city is big’. Hɔspansani foforo bi a wosua no mmara no ntew nnyinasoɔ ‘there is/are’ anaa wɔde asɛm no akyi de kyerɛdeɛ no, sɛnea ɛte wɔ ‘the city big’ na ɛnyɛ ‘the big city’.
rule:
Sɛ wopɛ sɛ woka kuan mu nwoma ne nniee no wɔ Twirekronkan A2 asɛm no, hwɛ mmarani yi:

1. **Kyerɛdeɛ + ‘to be’ (am/is/are) + kyerɛdeɛ**: Kasa kyerɛdeɛ a ɛte paa. Kyekyekye: 'My town is small.' (Mi pueblo es pequeño).
   - Sɛ ɛyɛ pronombres no: I am, you are, he/she/it is, we are, they are.
   - De kyerɛdeɛ no mfe asɛm no mu sɛ wode ama no: 'a big city', na ɛnyɛ 'a city big'.

2. **There is / There are**: Ma woka sɛ ɛyɛ dɛn wɔ kuan mu no.
   - There is + nkɔsoɔ/deɛ ɛyɛ nkɔsoɔ a ɛnyɛ deɛ wɔaka ho asɛm no: 'There is a park.' (Hay un parque).
   - There are + mmiɛnsa: 'There are two schools.' (Hay dos escuelas).
   - Sɛ ɛnyɛ: There isn't / There aren't: 'There isn't a cinema.' (No hay cine).
   - Sɛ ɛyɛ asɛm: Is there...? Are there...? (¿Hay...?).

3. **Preposiciones de lugar**: Ma wode ama sɛ wɔyɛ dɛn wɔ nna nea ɛwɔ hɔ.
   - 'in the center' (en el centro), 'on the corner' (en la esquina), 'near' (cerca de), 'next to' (al lado de).

4. **Verbos de acción**: 'You can see', 'you can find', 'there is' de ma woka sɛ ‘se puede encontrar’. 

5. **Conectores**: Hwɛ ‘and’ ma woyɔn asɛm ne ‘but’ ma wofa asɛm: 'My town is small but beautiful.' (Mi pueblo es pequeño pero bonito).

Sɛ ɛyɛ A2 no, ma wode asɛm no yɛ nkɔsoɔ ne yɛ dɛn so. Nka sɛ ‘there is’ mmiɛnsa no yɛ ‘there are’ – na ɛnyɛ ‘there is many shops’.

translations.tw: Kasa kuan mu nwoma ne nniee

title: Talking About Hobbies / Kasa kɛ w’ayɛ anadwo
bridge: Wɔ Twi mu, sɛ yɛbɛka kɛseɛ ne anadwo a, yɛnkyɛnkyɛ yɛbɔ mmara ‘gustar’ anaa ‘encantar’ ne kyerɛw kronkron (’me gusta’, ’te gusta’), na ɛno akyi yɛkae ‘me gusta + infinitivo’. Wɔ English mu, mmara ‘like’ rekɔ so paa: ‘I like + -ing’ anaa ‘I like + to + mmara’. Nkɔso ntɛm atɛnnu bi ara nso ɛha, ɛno ne sɛ wɔ English mu yɛnntɔn asɛm biara ne nnɛmpoano a wɔde bɔ adwene kɛseɛ mu wɔ mmerɛ bɔ no wɔ mmerɛ kɛseɛ a wɔkae ‘on Mondays’ (los lunes), na wɔ Twi mu yɛde ‘los lunes’ ka paa. Afei, wɔ English mu yɛde ‘do’ kɔso kyerɛw kɛseɛ (’What do you do in your free time?’), na wɔ Twi mu yɛkae ‘¿Qué haces en tu tiempo libre?’.
rule: Sɛ wubɛka kɛseɛ wɔ English mu (A2): bɔ mmara ‘like’, ‘love’, ‘enjoy’ anaa ‘prefer’ akyi ne nneɛma anaa mmara wɔ -ing form mu (e.g. ‘I like music’, ‘I love playing soccer’). Wɔde ‘be interested in’ + nneɛma anaa -ing form (e.g. ‘I'm interested in photography’) nso. Sɛ wubɛkɔso a, de ‘What do you like doing?’ anaa ‘What do you do in your free time?’. Sɛ wubɛka mmerɛ a, de mmerɛ kyerɛw mmara bɔ ‘always’, ‘usually’, ‘sometimes’, ‘never’ akyi (e.g. ‘I usually read’). Wɔde prepositions ‘in’ (in my free time), ‘on’ (on weekends, on Mondays) ne ‘at’ (at home, at the weekend – wɔ British English mu) nso. Nhyira: wɔmmɔde ‘do’ ne ‘like’ wɔ present simple mu sɛ wuka kyerɛkyerɛ (yɛkae ‘I like’, na yɛnkae ‘I do like’ gyan sɛ yɛbɛkɔso kyerɛkyerɛ).

concept_examples.text: I like listening to music.
concept_examples.translation: Mɛgusta mfonini asɛm.

concept_examples.text: She loves playing tennis.
concept_examples.translation: Ɔbaa no ara nso pɛ tennisi.

concept_examples.text: What do you do in your free time?
concept_examples.translation: Wodeɛnso wuyɛ anadwo?
concept_examples.phonetic: /wɒt duː juː duː ɪn jɔː friː taɪm/

concept_examples.text: I usually go hiking on weekends.
concept_examples.translation: Mepɛ mmerɛ no mma mɛtwa.

common_error.explanation: Ɛbɔ nea ɛbɛyɛ sɛ wɔ Twi mu yɛkae ‘me gusta jugar’ de infinitivo, na mmusua no de kwan sii English mu. Nanso, wɔ English mu, afe ‘like’, ‘love’, ‘enjoy’ etc. akyi, yɛde -ing form anaa yɛntɔn ‘to’ ne infinitivo (na yɛnntɔn infinitivo gyan ‘to’). Sɛ wubɛtwa a, kyerɛ: afe ‘like’ no, de -ing form: ‘I like playing’. Wɔde ‘I like to play’ nso, nanso ɛnyɛ paa.

examples.original: I love reading books.
examples.note: De ‘love’ + -ing sɛ wubɛka kɛseɛ paa. Wɔ Twi mu yɛde ‘encantar’.

examples.original: She enjoys painting.
examples.note: ’Enjoy’ ntɛm ara ne -ing. Yɛnkae ‘enjoy to paint’.

examples.original: I don't like cooking.
examples.note: Sɛ wubɛka kyerɛkyerɛ a, de ‘don't’ + like + -ing. Wɔ Twi mu: ‘no me gusta’.

examples.original: What do you like doing?
examples.note: ɛno ne kwan paa a wɔde kɔso kɛseɛ. Wɔ Twi mu: ‘¿Qué te gusta hacer?’

examples.original: Do you play any sports?
examples.note: De ‘play’ ne pɔnkɛseɛ a ɛso ntɛm (play football, play tennis). Wɔ Twi mu: ‘jugar’.

examples.original: How often do you go to the cinema?
examples.phonetic: /haʊ ˈɒfən duː juː ɡəʊ tə ðə ˈsɪnəmə/
examples.note: Wɔ Twi mu yɛde ‘ir al cine’ ne ‘a’; na wɔ English mu yɛde ‘go to + lugar’.

examples.original: I often watch TV in the evening.
examples.phonetic: /aɪ ˈɒfən wɒtʃ ˌtiːˈviː ɪn ðə ˈiːvnɪŋ/
examples.note: Mmerɛ kyerɛw mmara (often, usually, always) rekɔ mmara a ɛso ntɛm. Wɔ Twi mu yɛkae ‘a menudo’.

examples.original: I prefer playing video games to reading.
examples.phonetic: /aɪ prɪˈfɜː ˈpleɪɪŋ ˈvɪdiəʊ ɡeɪmz tə ˈriːdɪŋ/
examples.note: Sɛ wubɛtwee kɛseɛ a, de ‘prefer A to B’, ne nnipa mmienu no wɔ -ing. Wɔ Twi mu: ‘prefiero X a Y’.

examples.original: On Sundays, I usually go for a walk.
examples.phonetic: /ɒn ˈsʌndeɪz aɪ ˈjuːʒuəli ɡəʊ fər ə wɔːk/
examples.note: De ‘on’ ne nnɛmpoano a ɛso ntɛm. Wɔ Twi mu yɛkae ‘los domingos’.
